sentences.text: Pycnonemosaurus is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur belonging to the family Abelisauridae, distinguished by a small pubic foot and a hatchet-shaped cnemial crest on the tibia.
The type specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — represents an immature individual, likely a subadult, of uncertain ontogenetic stage.
Later analyses estimate the animal was about 8.9 meters long, surpassing initial estimates of 6-7 meters, while another estimation suggests it reached a length of 9 meters and a weight of 3.6 tons.

The name Pycnonemosaurus nevesi is derived from Greek words meaning 'dense pastures and woods lizard', with the specific name 'nevesi' honoring Dr. Iedo Batista Neves, who died in 2000 and encouraged paleontological studies.
Fossil evidence suggests this predator likely preyed on titanosaurs found in the same locality.
The species Pycnonemosaurus nevesi was scientifically described by Kellner and Campos in 2002 after remains were discovered by farm owner Max de Barros Erhart and his workers at the Paulo Creek site.
The most important find was an incomplete skeleton of a large abelisaurid theropod found near titanosaurid sauropod bones.
Only one fossil occurrence of Pycnonemosaurus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
Its small, sharp teeth were used to grip struggling prey while the abelisaur shook and tore them apart.
Pycnonemosaurus was a predator that fed on medium-sized sauropodomorphs, small crocodylomorphs, and dromaeosaurs.

Pycnonemosaurus is classified as a member of Abelisauridae, a family of large predators within Abelisauria that dominated Gondwanan continents in the late Cretaceous, and Abelisauria belongs to Ceratosauria, a lineage that split early from other theropods.
The parent group of the genus Pycnonemosaurus is Furileusauria.
Recent phylogenetic analysis suggests a strong relationship between Pycnonemosaurus and the derived abelisaurids Carnotaurus and Aucasaurus.
A synonym for the genus Pycnonemosaurus is Pycnomenosaurus.
Pycnonemosaurus lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage, though it lived from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
There is a debate regarding the geological formation of the fossils, with initial assignments to the Bauru Group or Cambambe Formation later reassigned to the Cachoeira do Bom Jardim Formation.
